Optimal.Notes: Rendering at 1152x720 with FSR to 1280x800 gives a sharp, near-native image while keeping the GPU well within budget; the game's art style means high textures and shadows make a noticeable difference. This profile represents the sweet spot that most platinum reporters are likely using.

profiles.Summary: Persona 5 Royal is a stylish turn-based RPG with relatively modest PC requirements, making it an excellent fit for the Steam Deck — the RDNA 2 GPU comfortably exceeds the minimum spec and can drive the game at native resolution with high settings. It holds Verified status on Steam Deck and ProtonDB reporters rate it platinum, indicating a smooth out-of-the-box experience with minimal tinkering needed.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 650 Ti–760 range, well below the Deck's ~GTX 1050 Ti class GPU) and the game's Verified status and platinum ProtonDB tier. On your first run, confirm the 60 fps cap holds in Palace combat and busy Shibuya streets — if it dips, drop to the Optimal profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 7 W TDP with a lowered GPU clock and FSR upscaling from 960x600, the Deck sips power while keeping P5R's stylish visuals very presentable. The 30/40 Hz cap eliminates frame pacing wobble entirely.

KnownIssues: Some players report occasional stuttering during busy cutscenes or area transitions, particularly at higher quality settings.
The game's launcher may require dismissal before the main game starts; using the 'Play' option directly avoids most issues.
Audio sync issues have occasionally been reported in cutscenes under certain Proton versions; using the default or Proton Experimental resolves this for most users.
Frame pacing can be inconsistent if an uncapped frame rate is used; a 60 fps cap is strongly recommended for smoothness.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At native 1280x800 with all quality settings maxed and TDP uncapped, P5R runs at a locked 60 fps on the Deck — the GPU is comfortably above minimum spec for this title. Battery life is reduced significantly, so this is best for docked or plugged-in play.

Optimal.Notes: Persona 5 Royal's engine is light enough to hit a locked 60 fps at native resolution with high settings, delivering the intended visual experience. Motion blur is disabled as it can feel excessive on a handheld screen.

profiles.Summary: Persona 5 Royal is a stylish turn-based RPG with a distinctive 2D/3D art style that is well within the Steam Deck's capabilities, running smoothly at 60 fps with minimal tuning. The game is Steam Deck Verified with a strong platinum ProtonDB rating, indicating an excellent out-of-the-box experience on Deck.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck configuration reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 650 Ti–760 class, well below the Deck's GPU), the game's verified status, and its lightweight stylized engine. On first run, confirm the frame rate holds at 60 fps in Palaces and busy Tokyo areas — the game is expected to be well within the Deck's capabilities.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 6W TDP with a reduced render resolution and FSR upscaling, the Deck sips power while keeping the game perfectly playable. The stylized art style holds up well even at lower resolutions.

KnownIssues: Some players report minor stuttering during the first launch or shader compilation; subsequent sessions are smooth.
HDR output is not natively supported under Proton, so the OLED HDR panel runs in SDR mode.
Occasional audio desync reported in cutscenes by a small number of users.

MaxPerformance.Notes: With no TDP or GPU clock limits the Deck can push well above 60 fps in many scenes, taking advantage of the OLED's 90 Hz panel for extra smoothness. Battery life drops noticeably but the game remains fully playable.
